notes: §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR7: 'Within a USE procedure, there must not be the execution of any statement that would cause the execution of a USE procedure that had previously been invoked and had not yet returned control to the invoking routine'; no result is stated. EmitRunUseBody guards each procedure with __useActive[id]: an active procedure is not re-invoked (FlowUseError, EC-FLOW-USE, cannot be enabled at 85), and a different one is. Probes at 85: an OPEN EXTEND failing (35) inside its own file's USE procedure, and an EXTEND-phrase USE that fails on the first file, both return without re-entry, looping or abend; the witness's USE A invoking USE B prints USE A 35, USE B 35.

next.reason: 1985: "there must not be the execution of any statement that would cause the execution of a USE procedure that had previously been invoked"; 2023: "if a statement raises an exception condition that would cause the execution of a USE procedure ... the EC-FLOW-USE exception condition is set to exist". 1985 forbids such execution, leaving the result unspecified. 2023 defines a result: the EC-FLOW-USE exception condition is set to exist.
